source.stem:
The structures of four molecules are shown.

Which molecules belong to the same homologous series?

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Sugar: insoluble in water. Sand: soluble in water.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Neither soluble nor insoluble—solubility applies only to solids.

intelligence.enrichment: Some materials completely disappear when mixed in water; these materials dissolve and are soluble in water. Other materials do not mix with water and are insoluble. Some liquids completely mix with water, while others form a separate layer when left undisturbed. observed mixing behavior in water -> soluble, insoluble, or separate-layer outcome The learner correctly applies this rule: Some materials completely disappear when mixed in water; these materials dissolve and are soluble in water. Other materials do not mix with water and are insoluble. Some liquids completely mix with water, while others form a separate layer when left undisturbed. If stirring changes how water looks, the added material has dissolved.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 6 Science question. Chapter: Materials around us. The student must decide: When a material is mixed with water, decide whether it is soluble or insoluble from whether it dissolves completely. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Rewrite the figure and the stem so they agree. Exactly one visual. Recalculate the key. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE. If the stem numbers activities 1..n, every number must appear in an option (or in a structured part's first-class options). Two-tier (choose, then reason) is welcome: put A/B/C on part.options, not typed into part text.
